reason: Quote supports a limit of ten SCPs per OU for OUs in the landing zone, but the qualifier 'not adjustable' (rendered for a limit) is not stated, and the same page history notes self-service quota adjustments.
Quote supports up to 100 control-related operations in progress in total, console or API, for concurrent optional control activation and deactivation; the qualifier 'not adjustable' is not stated.
Quote supports up to 10,000 accounts in the landing zone's organization, divided among all OUs; the qualifier 'not adjustable' is not stated.
Quote supports up to five account-related operations in progress in Account Factory and unmanaging one account at a time; the qualifier 'not adjustable' is not stated.
Quote states Account Factory (or vending machine) is built as an abstraction on top of provisioned products in AWS Service Catalog.

Quotes state Account Factory is a configurable account template standardizing provisioning with pre-approved configurations, and it can create and enroll accounts and automates applying controls and policies.
Quote states best practices recommend multiple accounts, which act as isolated resource containers offering workload categorization and blast radius reduction.

Quotes support that accounts created outside Account Factory are not bound by the registered OU's controls and that outside accounts and OUs are not bound unless registered or enrolled, but the page frames this for organizations without a landing zone set up, and the claim drops that framing and applies the 'unless' to quote 1, which has none.

Quotes state the optional auto-enrollment is for landing zones 3.1 and above, the account automatically receives baseline resources and control configurations of the destination OU, for existing and newly created accounts.

Quotes, under the auto-enrollment steps, state moving into a registered OU gives baseline and controls for existing and new accounts, and moving to an unregistered OU or root unenrolls with automatic removal.
Quote states Organizations and IAM Identity Center come at no additional charge and you pay by usage for Service Catalog, CloudTrail, Config, CloudWatch, SNS, S3 and VPC.
Quotes state Norstella provisions accounts with infrastructure as code instead of multiple teams and uses Control Tower automation to align infrastructure of acquired businesses.

Quotes support the five-provider merger, Control Tower used to complete the migration in under 5 months, and a process that typically takes over 1 year; but they say Norstella used AWS (not Control Tower) to build an enterprise cloud environment, and 'multi-account' is not in the quotes.
History row dated May 20, 2024 states an increase of the concurrent control operations quota to 100.
History row dated August 30, 2024 states Control Tower supports up to 1000 accounts per OU, an increase of the limit.
History row dated October 15, 2025 states automatic account enrollment and moving between OUs.
History row dated November 25, 2024 states integration with AWS Backup to set up plans to back up Control Tower resources.
History row dated December 1, 2024 states preventive controls with declarative policies, a new type of policy for a new type of preventive control.
History row dated July 29, 2022 states version 3.0 changes from account-based to organization-based CloudTrail trails and enables aggregating Config information in the home Region only.
History row dated November 17, 2025 states landing zone 4.0 is available with optional service integrations and a dedicated controls environment.
History row dated January 24, 2023 states proactive controls moved from preview to general availability.
History row dated November 15, 2024 states managed resource control policies launched, a new type of preventive controls implemented with RCPs.
Quote and its next sentence state a control applies to an entire OU, every account in it is affected, and users are always subject to their account's OU controls.
Quotes state preventive controls use SCPs, RCPs and declarative policies, detective controls use Config rules, proactive controls use CloudFormation hooks.
Quote states detective controls detect noncompliance and alert through the dashboard, status clear, in violation or not enabled, and apply only in Regions Control Tower supports.
Quote states integrated detective Security Hub CSPM controls use Config rules and are owned by the Service-Managed Standard: AWS Control Tower.

Quotes support automatic drift detection and SNS notifications aggregated in the audit account, but not that resolving drift is a regular task for management account administrators, and the claim drops the note that these SNS notifications are not available when auto-enroll is enabled.

Quotes support that most drift can be resolved, deleting the Security OU prompts an immediate landing zone reset, and Move Account drift needs a landing zone update; deleting required roles is only in unquoted context.
Quote states Control Tower offers the easiest way to set up and govern a secure, compliant, multi-account environment based on best practices.
Quote supports 100 concurrent EnableControl and DisableControl operations with 10 in progress and the rest queued; the qualifier 'not adjustable' is not stated.
Quotes state an enrolled account must have the AWSControlTowerExecution role, must not have existing Config resources, and cannot become audit or log archive except during initial setup.
Quotes support mandatory controls through the OU's SCPs, Config recording all resources, and detective Config rules; baselining with Control Tower stack sets is not in any quote.
Quote states ephemeral workloads in Control Tower accounts may increase Config costs because Config records the create and delete changes.
Quotes state one landing zone per organization, the existing management account is used, and two new accounts (audit and logging) are set up in a registered OU.
Quote states orchestration extends Organizations and Control Tower applies controls (guardrails) to keep organizations and accounts from drift from best practices.
FAQ answer to 'Is there an API available' says yes, see the API reference, and use the console for all other operations.
Organizations FAQ answer about Control Tower states it is built on Organizations, sets up account structures automatically, and implements preventive guardrails with SCPs and RCPs.
FAQ quote names CfCT and AFT as solutions to add customizations to Control Tower accounts with CloudFormation templates, SCPs or Terraform.
FAQ quotes state the services are complementary and you should use Control Tower preventive controls with Security Hub detective controls.
FAQ quotes state Control Tower can customize new and existing accounts when provisioning from the console and customized accounts are provisioned in account factory.
